title: screen-map/v1 body
description: A screen a person can capture and paste — the closed list a classifier is allowed to answer from. One document per screen, exactly like fab-line and domain-skill, so a screen is added or retired by pushing or archiving one document instead of editing a shared array. The consumer (fdc-agent-be#63) hands this whole catalog to a vision model and then throws away any id the model made up, so the list is not a hint: it is the answer space. There are no tiered-value slots — a screen either exists in the system or it does not, and nothing here is a claim awaiting review. The id is body.id so a lister knows every screen without fetching each body.

id.description: The value a confirmed classification carries downstream. Lowercase kebab because it is also the document id, and the store keeps one case.

name.description: What the screen is called where people work. Spliced into a single rendered line — no newline, no leading markdown block marker.

program.description: The application the screen belongs to (FDC Monitor, SPC). Consumers group by this string WITHOUT normalising it, so two spellings split into two groups — keep the wording identical across documents.

menuPath.description: Where the screen sits under its program, outermost first. Joined with the program into one caption line, so it is a trail rather than a sentence.

hints.description: What the screen LOOKS like — the only field that changes how well classification works, because it is what the vision model reads beside the capture. Write what is visibly distinctive (a chart above a table, a UCL line, a filter form), not what the screen is for; purpose does not survive a screenshot.

expectedColumns.description: What a table extracted from this screen should contain. Not consumed yet — the extraction step (fdc-agent-be#63 follow-up) reads it; the classifier ignores it.
